objective: Build an owned-model LFG developer prototype grounded in real user corrections and observed outcomes, with local and hosted paths and future RRFlow/SWAG integration.

evidence.claim: Records source state, actual Spark observations, current boundaries and research.
A private source-bound review workflow exists.
Defines the private local feedback security, record, revision and tests contract.

constraints: Follow AGENTS.md and newer user instructions; preserve existing user work.
Training on authorized private projects and conversations may continue; gates affect trust and promotion, not permission to train.
Keep private datasets, conversations, weights and secrets local and out of Git; review secret screening.
Models, runtime limits, policies and integrations must be configurable; preserve extension fields.
Do not claim a trained quality-qualified model, network security, integration or benchmark without evidence.
Inspect and preserve all unrelated tracked, untracked and user-created work.
authorized_scope: Modify the listed task paths to implement the selected ready task and its tests.
Use the owner-authorized local projects and conversations within the privacy constraints.
Read local service and checkpoint status; avoid changing or terminating running jobs without task-specific justification.

tasks.title: Persist and review real assessment corrections
steps: Read docs/lfg/FEEDBACK-JOURNAL-DESIGN.md and inspect the current server, kernel journal, private review ledger, assessment and UI. Preserve all unrelated tracked and untracked work.

Implement the versioned local feedback record, transactional durable revisions, optimistic concurrency and append-only rollback exactly as specified. Preserve extra fields and distinguish original recommendation, owner correction and confirmed or unknown outcome.

Implement disabled-by-default private storage and loopback-only API access, with the specified host, origin and session-token protections; hosted authorization is explicitly out of scope. Fail closed if privacy or listener identity cannot be established.
Add developer UI create, reopen, revise and rollback with visible provenance and unknown state. Keep raw prompt capture disabled unless explicitly configured.
Add the design-specified API/UI tests and configuration documentation; record actual test results and escalate any design or platform boundary that cannot be met.

checks.expected: All relevant server tests pass, including persistence, revisions and access boundaries.
UI tests pass including feedback interaction.

acceptance: The complete record and access contract in docs/lfg/FEEDBACK-JOURNAL-DESIGN.md is implemented and tested, including persistence across restart, conflict handling, extensions, rollback, concurrent writes, permission failures, local-only and origin restrictions.
The UI distinguishes recommendations, corrections and confirmed or unknown outcomes and reports unavailable feedback.
No private data or session tokens are logged or committed; raw prompt content is not retained by default.

tasks.title: Connect and inspect an experimental owned-model assessment
steps: Inspect existing owned-byte runtime and model artifact contract.
Add configurable, explicitly selected model backend with bounded input, output and execution time, explicit malformed, truncated, unavailable and timeout states; retain deterministic assessment.
Show engine identity, checkpoint provenance and results side by side in the developer UI; capture actual failures.

checks.expected: Backend tests pass, including failures and limits.

acceptance: Run a real owned-model inference and record its actual output and artifact hash, or document the concrete operational blocker.
No synthetic output is represented as model output; deterministic behavior remains selectable.

tasks.title: Prepare private, source-grounded supervision and held-out data
steps: Reuse source-bound review ledger and ingest real corrections and verified outcomes with provenance.
Recover and connect the authored questions and templates; distinguish unknown facts and proposals from confirmed labels.
Version private datasets, scan and review secrets, deduplicate and split by independent project or conversation.
acceptance: Produce auditable private dataset and split manifests with no secrets or personal source content committed.
Training and evaluation examples have traceable target provenance.

tasks.title: Score real assessments against independent targets
steps: Create real model predictions and evaluate field-by-field against adjudicated held-out targets.
Record coverage, missing targets, error categories, model identifiers and comparison with deterministic and teacher baselines.
Keep tuning data separate from final holdout; continue authorized training independent of quality promotion.
acceptance: Produce a versioned reproducible scorecard with actual predictions and non-synthetic targets or report the specific unavailable data.

tasks.title: Measure and improve runtime and Spark training
steps: Profile real CPU and Spark workloads with artifact IDs, input distributions, p50/p95 latency, memory, throughput and reproducible configuration.
Develop original model architecture and distillation experiments; compare quality, size, CPU and accelerator tradeoffs.
Make persistent training resumable, observable and resource-bounded with explicit failure and stop states.
acceptance: A reproducible run proves actual training progress and captures measured performance; no unsupported 650 MB release claim.

tasks.title: Integrate, secure and package the standalone product
steps: Implement versioned extensible interfaces for RRFlow, SWAG and MCP with configurable standalone and hosted use.
Implement authenticated remote access, signed updates and rollback as supported by the product design.
Build and verify a clean executable and actual model artifact for documented targets.
acceptance: Demonstrate standalone and authorized integration flows and record binary, model, benchmark and update evidence.

escalation_triggers: Relevant source anchor changed or Git baseline is no longer an ancestor.
Scope conflicts with current user direction or a later instruction.
Privacy, access control or data provenance cannot be resolved within authorized scope.
Repeated test failure, unexpected side effects, missing real artifact or unsupported runtime capability.
The requested task requires an unapproved external communication or unverified claim.
